about.title: Nevada City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Nevada City's mix of narrow, winding roads and busy corridors like SR-49 and State Route 20 means collisions happen even in a town this small. Recent records show 11 injury collisions and 14 people hurt in a single year here, with Monday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. showing up often in the reports — likely tied to commuters and end-of-day traffic squeezing through town. Whether you were driving, a passenger, or on foot near one of these corridors, the aftermath can mean medical bills, missed work, and confusing calls from insurance adjusters. LawProactive isn't a law firm, but we connect people hurt in Nevada City crashes with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the claim, deal with insurers, and explain your options under California law. There's no cost to get connected, and any attorney in our network works on contingency, meaning no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Back

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government road or vehicle was involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Your Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by the percentage of blame assigned to you — even if that share is small. Having someone review the crash details before you speak with the other driver's insurer can help protect your share of any recovery.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but insurers still push back hard on these claims. An independent attorney can help document your losses and avoid giving a recorded statement that could later be used against you.

items.question: I was in a crash on SR-49 near Nevada City — should I talk to the other driver's insurance company first?
items.answer: It's generally safer to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can shift blame or minimize your injuries. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Nevada County?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, like the county or state, was involved in causing the crash, that deadline can be as short as six months. It's worth getting a quick evaluation early so you don't miss a critical date.

items.question: What does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront fee to speak with someone about your Nevada City car accident.
